questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.topic: Major Centralised States in Pre-colonial Nigeria
questions.subtopic: Historical and later seats of Oyo
questions.learningObjective: Locate Old Oyo and distinguish the historic capital site from a later seat.
questions.prompt: The heritage submission places Old Oyo at approximately 9° N, 4.4° E. Find its marker and use both coordinates to explain why R is a poor match.
questions.answer: P marks Old Oyo. R is much farther south and also farther east than the location given.
questions.explanation: P fits both the latitude and the longitude in the source. Old Oyo is shown by a representative point within the submitted coordinate range.

markingGuide.description: Uses latitude to rule out R.
Uses longitude to rule out R.

stimulus.title: Three centres on a coordinate map
stimulus.textAlternative: North is up and east is right. P is near 9.0° N, 4.4° E. Q is near 12.0° N, 8.5° E. R is near 6.3° N, 5.7° E. Markers are approximate reference points. The map has no territorial boundaries.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.topic: Major Centralised States in Pre-colonial Nigeria
questions.subtopic: Historical and later seats of Oyo
questions.learningObjective: Locate Old Oyo and distinguish the historic capital site from a later seat.
questions.prompt: A caption labels Old Oyo and the later capital founded at Ago d’Oyo as one site. Which revision is best supported?
questions.answer: Identify Old Oyo and Ago d’Oyo as different seats and say which period the map describes.
questions.explanation: Historical scholarship distinguishes Oyo-Ile from the later capital at Ago d’Oyo. A time-specific caption prevents readers from confusing the seats.
options: Treat every place named Oyo as a single site.
Identify Old Oyo and Ago d’Oyo as different seats and say which period the map describes.
Label the earlier site with the name of its later ruler instead of a location.
Omit all place names and use the outline of present-day Oyo State.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.topic: Major Centralised States in Pre-colonial Nigeria
questions.subtopic: Locating Kano and interpreting its landmarks
questions.learningObjective: Use a coordinate map and a heritage source to locate Kano as a historical centre.
questions.prompt: The locations of two centres are marked at P and Q. Q marks Kano and P marks Old Oyo. Describe Kano’s direction from Old Oyo. Name one feature from Nigeria’s heritage submission that helps locate the historical city within present-day Kano.
questions.answer: Kano lies north-east of Old Oyo. The ancient city walls, Dala Hill, Kurmi Market or the Emir’s Palace provide a named historical landmark.
questions.explanation: Kano is higher and farther right on the grid. The submitted landmarks help connect a general city reference point with the older urban landscape.

markingGuide.description: States north-east or gives both component directions.
Names a landmark listed in the submission.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.topic: Major Centralised States in Pre-colonial Nigeria
questions.learningObjective: Locate Benin City on a map and explain the limits of a centre marker.
questions.prompt: Use the locator and a gazetteer entry of about 6.3° N, 5.7° E to label the centre of the historical Kingdom of Benin. Compare its position with Old Oyo at P.
questions.answer: R is Benin City. Its latitude is lower and its longitude higher than P, so it lies south-east of Old Oyo.
questions.explanation: The gazetteer locates present-day Benin City, the centre named for the historical kingdom. The comparison follows the grid orientation.

markingGuide.description: Describes the south-east position relative to P.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.topic: Major Centralised States in Pre-colonial Nigeria
questions.learningObjective: Locate Benin City on a map and explain the limits of a centre marker.
questions.prompt: A pupil wants to colour every place between R at Benin City and P at Old Oyo as territory of the Kingdom of Benin. Explain why the two point locations are insufficient. Describe one additional type of historical evidence the pupil should seek.
questions.answer: R and P show where two centres were. They do not show where political authority extended between them at a particular time. The pupil could seek a dated historical map or a historian’s account based on records of territories under the kingdom’s authority.
questions.explanation: Mapping an area of control requires evidence about territory and period. Knowing a centre’s position only gives a point.

markingGuide.description: Explains that markers locate centres rather than territorial extent.
Suggests suitable evidence tied to a historical period.
